Honestly it's a shame how the game turned out, the writing is absolutely the biggest flaw of Andromeda without a doubt, well that and the non-combat animation work imo. It legit looks like something went wrong when they did the mocapping and rigging, every humanoid character has broad hunched up shoulders and don't move their arms correctly when walking or running.

That's not even to mention the automated lipsync animations which are rightfully notorious, patches did improve them but those base issues still remain. It doesn't help that a majority of the human characters are downright ugly or just look like plastic, thankfully the aliens look remarkably better (as long as you don't think about how many Turians are bleached white in this game for some reason)

The gameplay is alright though, its fun enough as a modern take on the old Mass Effect cover-based shooting. There's a larger focus on powers & abilties as well as mixing around class archetypes, but despite this you can only have 3 powers at a time?? When in the original games you can just have all your powers lined up in a nice pop-up wheel??? It's a WEIRD decision that kinda messes with how much fun the combat can be... there ARE the profiles which work around this limit but it's still a weird choice to make, having to choose a profile first instead of simply selecting the power you want to use.

Anyways... pointless rambling over, Vetra is the best part of this entire game - no question - but even she isn't worth it. Modern BioWare SUCKS and I do not trust them with Mass Effect 4 lmao

I dont know why the game has a bad name, i played and beat Mass Effect 1 and loved it, Mass Effect 2 was a huge dissapointment to me, decided to give this one a go 3 years after i played the first 2, and i love the game, open world space exploration sci-fi game is something that i find very intriguing and fun, gameplay is top notch, and i also like the plot and sense of novelty. Its a good game id rate it 8/10, would be better if you were able to hotkey more than 3 quick actions (biotics, grenades etc.) so far i havent seen other downsides, and this is not a deal breaker at all

Could have been a lot better. But it is a solid game in 2024, despite the release drama.

The opening premise was actually a breath of fresh air and it blows things wide open. I found myself swept up with excitement by the possibilities of an entirely new galaxy enriched with the existing Mass Effect lore and easter eggs. Narratively it allows a clean-break from the Shepard - Reaper - Prothean narrative whilst also honouring and acknowledging it subtly. Sadly the early potential of Andromeda's pioneering spirit is ultimately hamstrung, by a story that does what it needs to do, nothing more, and more importantly, the Angara apparently being the only native friendly highly-advanced species. But despite that, combat is ultimately fun.

If the game wasn't abandoned and had more time in the oven, it may have stood a chance against the following shortcomings which really held it back:

- Character models look awful
- Cutscenes are painful
- Characters themselves aren't as memorable as the roster from Mass Effect 1 to 3
- Voice acting is poor throughout. Krogan and Salarian NPCs sound particularly bad.
- Not enough races/species

Ultimately I would have liked to see an expansion to this game, or even a direct sequel to Andromeda with a much more vibrant galactic community on a fully realised Nexus. It has the bones of a very good game, just a lot of systems are half-baked.
Hardest part of this game is probably the first few hours.  It ramps up really slowly, combat wise.  Gets more fun as you go, and there's new game + available.
